newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Englishman victim of "explosive anger", court told.
newsitem.headline: Englishman victim of "explosive anger", court told.

text.p: An English tourist killed at Sydney's Bondi Beach last year had been savagely beaten and was then hit by a bus, a court was told on Monday.
However, prosecutor Chris Maxwell said it was unclear whether 28-year-old London postman Brian Hagland had been running away or was thrown into the path of the bus by his attacker.

In his opening address at the start of the committal hearing of Aaron Lee Martin, 23, who has been charged with Hagland's murder, Maxwell said the defendant was in a "mood of explosive phyiscal anger".
"He was looking for someone or something to take it one," Maxwell told Sydney's Downing Centre Local court.
Hagland died from head and internal injuries after he was assaulted in a street attack witnessed by his fiancee in the early hours of Saturday, September 7 last year.
His fiancee, Connie Casey, 25, has said two men kicked and punched Hagland to death in an unprovoked attack near Australia's best known beach.
Neither Martin nor Sean Leigh Cushman, 23, who has been charged with being an accessory after the fact, entered a plea.
